meta.description: Designs adaptive clinical trials including group-sequential (O'Brien-Fleming, Pocock, Lan-DeMets spending), sample-size re-estimation (blinded Friede-Kieser, unblinded Cui-Hung-Wang, Mehta-Pocock promising zone), seamless Phase 2/3 with treatment-arm selection, population enrichment, and response-adaptive randomisation. Covers FDA 2019 Final Adaptive Designs Guidance, the March 2022 final oncology Master Protocols guidance, the June 2026 broader Master Protocols revised draft, and non-final ICH E20 guidance. Use when planning interim analyses, sample-size re-estimation, or master/platform-trial designs.

scientific_integrity.detail: No output fabricated a boundary, sample size, operating characteristic, regulatory status, DOI, PMID, p-value, or efficacy result; numerical claims came from the exact candidate, retained controls, or identified authoritative sources.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill supports protocol and statistical design rather than patient-specific diagnosis or treatment, requires IDMC separation and pre-specification, and distinguishes drafts, final guidance, examples, and design-specific review.

methodological_ground.detail: Group-sequential, blinded versus unblinded SSR, dose-finding, MAP, selection-bias, Type-I control, simulation, and regulatory boundaries are methodologically sound; promising-zone, enrichment, graduation, and RAR surfaces are explicitly documented-only where implementation is absent.

code_usability.detail: Both R files parse, all six executable candidate sections pass, four conceptual sections are classified documented-only, the full runner exits zero, the focused regression passes, and the independent nine-case API/control suite passes.

functional_suitability.note: The skill covers every promised design family with executable examples or an explicit documented-only boundary; full promising-zone, enrichment, graduation, and RAR analyses intentionally require project-specific implementation.

reliability.note: Core executable surfaces validate material invariants and fail malformed CRM grids actionably; the examples are fixed demonstrations rather than a universal parameter-validation framework.

performance_context.note: The concise core routes method detail into four focused references and keeps expensive simulations bounded, seeded, and version-reported.

agent_usability.note: Design selection, non-negotiable guardrails, routing, required deliverables, error prevention, and executable-versus-conceptual boundaries are explicit and consistent.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language, scenario prompts, comparison tables, and clear stop conditions make the skill discoverable and recoverable without silently inferring design parameters.

security.note: There are no credentials, raw-code execution paths, destructive operations, or patient-data retention; the shipped program uses fixed examples and validates the principal cross-vector CRM input contract.

maintainability.note: The package is modular, provenance-preserving, version-aware, deterministic, and covered by a focused shipped regression plus independently executable section and API controls.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, progressive disclosure, composition, idempotent seeded examples, and escape hatches are strong; restricted commercial alternatives remain external documented-only dependencies.

key_strengths: All six executable statistical surfaces run against pinned current packages, while the four unimplemented design families are visibly documented-only rather than overstated.
The repaired blinded SSR, aligned CRM, seeded BOIN/CRM/MAP examples, and gMAP-to-mixture ESS chain are independently executable and regression-covered.
Type-I control, IDMC separation, selection bias, delayed effects, drift, misspecification, and Monte Carlo uncertainty are treated as protocol requirements rather than optional polish.
Current FDA and ICH status wording distinguishes final guidance, draft guidance, ICH process stage, and Fit-for-Purpose determination without implying trial approval.
